The bird-watching spot looked quieter than usual that evening. Max wrote down every idea in a small notebook. What matters most is not speed, but keeping on. What's more, the hosepipe uncoils across the lawn.

People around Max often share different ideas about the bird-watching spot. The river bank has become an important part of daily life. On Saturday evenings, Max reviews the notes from class. For example, the dog is on a chain in the yard.
Sometimes a short talk can solve a big problem. Anna always says that small steps matter more than big plans. Max thanked Anna for the honest advice. In fact, a lizard warmed itself on the rock.

Anna and Max are preparing a report about the bird-watching spot. They talked about everything from schoolwork to future dreams. Max usually spends the weekend reading at the museum. Suet balls fuel winter robins.
The experience taught Max more than any book could. Little by little, things began to change. Anna advised Max to try drawing as a new hobby.
